answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, turning identity creation from free into costly. Trust then flows through a reputation graph: each vertex accumulates attestations only from peers with locked stakes, so fake nodes stay isolated at the graph edge. Cheap identities spiral into uselessness because they cannot borrow the reputation of honest agents, while a falcon-eyed audit trail of signed, timestamped attestations lets the network detect and prune clusters of colluding fakes before they drain the emission pool.
